question.problem: Given a rectangular pyramid, find the differential $\text{d}V$ for the volume $V$ of the rectangular pyramid if the base is a square with the side of $a=6$ and the height is $h=5.$
question.worked_solution:
The volume of the rectangular pyramid is $V=\frac{1}{3}{a}^{2}h.$ Let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(a,h) & =(\frac{∂V}{∂a})\,\text{d}a+(\frac{∂V}{∂h})\,\text{d}h \\  & =\frac{2ah}{3}\,\text{d}a+\frac{{a}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}h\end{aligned}
$$

For $a=6$ and $h=5,$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}V(6,5) & =\frac{2\cdot 6\cdot 5}{3}\,\text{d}a+\frac{{6}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}h \\  & =20\,\text{d}a+12\,\text{d}h.\end{aligned}
$$
